items.stem: A task in Microsoft Project does not move when you link a predecessor that finishes later. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The task is set to manually scheduled
options.rationale: Correct: manually scheduled tasks ignore dependency-driven date changes until switched to automatic.

options.text: Microsoft Project does not support task links
The predecessor has no resources assigned
options.rationale: Resource assignment does not control whether links move dates.
A baseline records a reference; it does not affect link-driven scheduling.

items.explanation: Correct: manually scheduled tasks ignore dependency-driven date changes until switched to automatic.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: You change a task's assignment units from 100% to 50% and want to understand the effect. Which TWO statements are correct for a fixed-units, effort-driven task? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Duration can lengthen because the same work is done at a lower rate
options.rationale: Correct: with fixed units and fixed work, reducing the rate extends duration.

options.text: Work stays the same unless you change it
options.rationale: Correct: the amount of work is held; only how it spreads over time changes.

options.text: Duration is unaffected by assignment units
options.rationale: Units directly influence duration for effort-driven, fixed-units tasks.

options.text: Work automatically halves when units halve
options.rationale: Work is not reduced by changing units; it is the planned effort.

items.explanation: Correct: with fixed units and fixed work, reducing the rate extends duration.

items.stem: At the halfway status date a task shows positive finish variance. What does this indicate against the baseline?

options.text: The task is forecast to finish later than the baseline planned
options.rationale: Correct: positive finish variance means the current finish is later than baseline.

options.text: The task finished earlier than planned
options.rationale: An earlier finish would show negative variance.
Variance requires a baseline to exist, so it has not been deleted.
Variance reflects dates, not resource assignment.

items.explanation: Correct: positive finish variance means the current finish is later than baseline.
